question: Of Americans born in the early 1980s, how many earn more than their parents did at the same age?
answer: About half. Chetty and colleagues found that about 90% of Americans born in 1940 out-earned their parents after inflation, but only about 50% of those born in the 1980s. Most of the fall came from growth flowing to the top, not slower growth. Out-earning one's parents stopped being the default.
move: An economy can grow while the typical person stops moving up.
ask: Am I measuring my progress against my parents, or against what the economy as a whole has gained?
trap: About 90%, since a growing economy lifts each new generation.
reference: Chetty, Grusky, Hell, Hendren, Manduca & Narang, The Fading American Dream: Trends in Absolute Income Mobility Since 1940, Science, 2017
